notes: Inspected all 10 current portable frames: the square battered base, two projecting stringcourses, elevated inland doorway, opposite sea window, flank loop, shallow parapet embrasures, western corner stair shelter, roof vent, drain and flagpole are intact.

The roof remains open behind the parapet; the shelter doorway opens onto it. Repair tints and individual stone courses distinguish the reconstructed upper and lower facade. No stray or floating geometry, visible holes in wall surfaces, or clipped apertures were found.

Inspected all 10 current shared sky-PMREM frames, including north-up placement. Raw limestone has subtle mineral variation without a second ashlar grid over the modeled joints. Pale repaired stone, recessed timber door and metal fittings retain their relative material character.

fidelityReview.notes: Finished detailed original exterior of the restored 2009 appearance using the custodian, the national inventory and original Joseph Psaila photographs. Modeled the battered stone base and joints, projecting cornices, raised door and hardware, sea window, flank loop, roof parapet and embrasures, restored stair shelter, roof vent, drain and pole. No target-specific surveyed elevation was published in the consulted inventory. Heights, aperture sizes, block pattern and small fittings are photographic reconstructions tied to the mapped plan. The internal rooms and spiral stair, temporary ladders, surrounding shoreline and adjacent World War II pillboxes are separate from the requested exterior model.
